en: The Philippine eagle, our national bird, features a unique shaggy crest and can hunt monkeys despite being an avian predator.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift bamboo incubator to save premature babies in rural areas lacking electricity.
Marcela Agoncillo and her daughter sewed the first official Philippine flag by hand while in exile in Hong Kong.
Ifugao ancestors engineered the Banaue Rice Terraces over two thousand years ago using an intricate irrigation system carved by hand.
The Philippine Supreme Court consists of fifteen justices, including the Chief Justice, who must mandatorily retire at exactly seventy years old.
The ancient Baybayin writing system uses a small cross or dot above or below a consonant to change its vowel sound.
Dancers in the Ati-Atihan festival paint their skin with black soot to honor the indigenous Ati people of Aklan.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polymath who spoke twenty-two languages and successfully performed eye surgery on his own mother.
The sampaguita, our national flower, gets its name from the romantic phrase 'sumpa kita,' which means 'I promise you.'
The traditional bayanihan practice involved an entire community physically carrying a heavy nipa hut on their shoulders to relocate it.
Andres Bonifacio founded the Katipunan, a secret society that used blood compacts and coded languages to fight Spanish colonizers.
Juan Luna spent eight months painting his masterpiece Spoliarium, which won the gold medal at an 1884 Madrid art exhibition.
